classification.difficultyReason: Students independently decompose the pool using differences in length and depth, calculate its capacity, then connect volume to filling rate and convert the resulting minutes into hours and minutes.

content.prompt:
The diagram shows an empty swimming pool.
Water flows into the pool at a rate of 600 litres per minute.
How long, in hours and minutes, will it take to fill the pool? (Hint: $1000\text{ L}=1\text{ m}^3$)

spec.description: Unshaded perspective pool with a level rim, a 10 m shallow flat floor and a sloping floor over the remaining 20 m. Three source right-angle markers are retained.
spec.mathematics: Length 30 m, width 12 m, shallow depth 1 m, deep depth 4 m; the longitudinal cross-section is a rectangle plus a triangle.
spec.answerVisibility: All dimensions are permanent givens; no calculated volume or time is shown.

answer.worked:
Split the pool into a rectangular prism and a triangular prism.
$$\begin{align*}V_1&=30\times12\times1=360\text{ m}^3\\V_2&=\frac12\times(30-10)\times(4-1)\times12=360\text{ m}^3\\V_{\text{tot}}&=360+360=720\text{ m}^3\\\text{Water required}&=720\times1000=720\,000\text{ L}\\\text{Time}&=\frac{720\,000}{600}=1200\text{ minutes}\\\text{Time}&=20\text{ hours }0\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$$
